candidate_relations.reason: Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia describes the underlying cardiac anatomy but does not address the thrombocytopenia mechanism (hypoxia-induced). The reference diagnosis is about the cause of thrombocytopenia.

candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record shows negative antiplatelet antibodies, negative platelet-associated immunoglobulins, and IVIg did not raise platelet count meaningfully, making ITP an incorrect etiology. The reference diagnosis is hypoxia-induced, not immune-mediated.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Asserts immune-mediated etiology which is explicitly excluded by the workup

candidate_relations.reason: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is a distinct genetic disorder with eczema, immunodeficiency, and microthrombocytes; no features support this diagnosis in the record.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Genetic immunodeficiency syndrome unrelated to hypoxia-induced thrombocytopenia

candidate_relations.reason: While surgery and prostaglandin may contribute transiently, the thrombocytopenia persists at 10 months (preoperatively, without recent surgery or prostaglandin), pointing to chronic hypoxia as the primary mechanism. This candidate misattributes the etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Attributes thrombocytopenia to surgery and prostaglandin rather than hypoxia

candidate_relations.reason: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia is a distinct genetic disorder; the clinical picture with fluctuating platelet counts correlating with hypoxia does not support this.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Congenital bone marrow failure syndrome unrelated to hypoxia

candidate_relations.reason: Jacobsen syndrome is a chromosomal disorder; no features in the record support this diagnosis.

candidate_relations.scope_detail: Thrombocytopenia attributed to cyanotic congenital heart disease (i.e., hypoxia) — matches reference
